facts.statement: Paracetamol is used for pain and high temperature in adults.
Metformin is used for type 2 diabetes and lowers blood glucose.
Metformin can be associated with vitamin B12 deficiency; this does not mean every user develops it.
Cetirizine is an antihistamine for allergy symptoms.
Cetirizine can cause sleepiness despite being classed as less drowsy.
Amoxicillin is a prescription penicillin antibiotic used for some bacterial infections.
Antibiotics do not treat viral colds or flu; this is not a personal treatment decision.
Antibiotic resistance concerns bacteria resisting an antibiotic, not the patient body becoming resistant.
An authorized human reviews extracted fields, documents and flags; the chatbot does not approve a case.
Printed-English local OCR may make mistakes; uncertain extraction needs correction against the original.
Identity matching considers generic/brand, strength and form; it does not establish interchangeability or regulatory approval.
A change to cited evidence can make an old answer stale; an unrelated edit need not do so.

sources.title: Paracetamol: general information
sources.excerpt: Paracetamol is used to relieve pain and reduce a high temperature in adults. Forms include tablets, capsules, liquid and suppositories. It is not suitable for everyone; kidney or liver conditions and a previous allergy require professional advice. Other cold-and-flu products may also contain paracetamol, creating a risk of accidental excess. Check the medicine leaflet and ask a pharmacist when unsure. This is general adult information, not an individual treatment or dose recommendation.

sources.title: Metformin: general information
sources.excerpt: Metformin is a prescription medicine commonly used for type 2 diabetes. It helps lower blood glucose. Treatment and monitoring depend on the individual and their other medicines and conditions. A clinician or pharmacist should advise on suitability or treatment changes. This educational summary does not recommend starting, stopping or changing a prescription.

sources.title: Metformin: possible side effects
sources.excerpt: Metformin can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, reduced appetite and altered taste. Vitamin B12 deficiency is another possible issue. Not everyone experiences side effects. Persistent or troublesome effects need a pharmacist or doctor. Rare serious problems include lactic acidosis and severe allergy; severe illness or breathing problems require urgent assessment. This summary is not a complete list or a diagnosis.

sources.title: Cetirizine: allergies and possible side effects
sources.excerpt: Cetirizine is an antihistamine used for allergy symptoms such as hay fever and hives. Although classed as a less-drowsy antihistamine, it can still cause sleepiness. Other possible common effects include headache, dry mouth, nausea, dizziness and diarrhoea. Do not drive if it makes you sleepy. Check the leaflet and ask a pharmacist about suitability. Brand names are not enough to identify an ingredient because different products in a brand family may contain different medicines.

sources.title: Amoxicillin: general antibiotic information
sources.excerpt: Amoxicillin is a prescription penicillin antibiotic used for certain bacterial infections. Nausea and diarrhoea are common possible side effects. A clinician decides whether an antibiotic is appropriate. This information does not establish that symptoms are bacterial and does not recommend a prescription, dose, substitution or treatment duration.

sources.title: Antibiotics and viral colds
sources.excerpt: Antibiotics act against bacteria, not the viruses responsible for colds and flu. Unnecessary antibiotic use contributes to resistance. Follow a qualified clinician on whether an antibiotic is needed and follow the prescription and leaflet. Do not share another person's antibiotics. Serious allergic reactions need urgent medical attention. This is general educational information, not an individual treatment decision. The source page has an older review date; check current local clinical guidance with a professional.

sources.title: Human-in-the-loop validation
sources.excerpt: Human-in-the-loop validation means an authorized pharmacist or claims reviewer checks extracted fields, source documents and risk signals before making a verification decision. The review actions are Verify, Return for Correction and Escalate. A reason and audit trail record the action. A chatbot answer cannot verify, reject, close or approve a case.

sources.title: Document upload and OCR correction
sources.excerpt: The current verification MVP accepts prescriptions, pharmacy invoices and claim forms as supported images or PDFs. Local Tesseract reads printed English text. OCR may misread medicine names, strengths, quantities, dates or amounts. Low-confidence extraction needs human confirmation against the original. PDF processing is bounded to three pages; omitted pages mean incomplete evidence, not a fully checked document.

sources.title: Medicine identity matching
sources.excerpt: Medicine identity resolution compares brand name, generic name, strength and dosage form against a small versioned academic catalogue. Similar brand names or a shared generic ingredient do not establish interchangeable medicines. Unresolved or ambiguous identity needs review. The academic catalogue is not live CDSCO regulatory verification and contains no verified stock, price or prescribing advice.

sources.title: Antibiotic resistance: definition
sources.excerpt: Antibiotic resistance means bacteria change so an antibiotic no longer controls them effectively. It is the bacteria, not the person’s body, that become resistant. This is general education; it does not identify an infection or select treatment.

sources.title: Antibiotic resistance: prevention and scope
sources.excerpt: Unnecessary or incorrect antibiotic use contributes to resistance. Antibiotics do not treat viral colds. A qualified clinician decides whether an antibiotic is appropriate. This is general stewardship information, not a prescription, dose or treatment-duration recommendation.

sources.title: Answer freshness and correction impact
sources.excerpt: A previous case answer remains historical text after a correction. Its signed evidence dependencies can be checked against the current case. A changed cited dependency can make that answer stale; an unrelated edit need not. Freshness is evidence-version consistency, not proof of clinical correctness.
